corpusSummary: Across 2026 records, the corpus documents a rapid expansion of social-science work on large language models, emphasizing methodological use, governance, and cross-domain impacts. Researchers probe LLM cognition and bias, interrogate trust and embodiment in human-AI interaction, harness LLMs for health misinformation, education, and policy analysis, and assess fairness, transparency, and ethical considerations. The studies reveal both promise (personalized pedagogy, participatory planning) and cautions (misinformation, dependency, and cultural relevance).

themes.name: AI as methodological instrument and governance
themes.description: A wave of studies shows LLMs as research tools and governance instruments for coding, analysis, simulations, and evaluation across health, policy, and education.

themes.name: Human-AI interaction, trust, and embodiment
themes.description: Papers examine trust, perceived humanness, embodiment (ADE), addiction risk, social capital, and the effects of anthropomorphism on behavior.

themes.name: AI in health, misinformation, and healthcare communication ethics
themes.description: Research investigates AI-driven misinformation spread, patient education, and clinician–patient communication, with equity and safety frameworks.

themes.name: AI in education: tutoring, scaffolding, assessment, and literacy
themes.description: Studies explore AI tutoring, agent-based scaffolding, AI-integrated curricula, and ethical implications for learning and assessment.
